Mesillat Yesharim 25:10: This is what King David used to pray, saying (Psalms 86:11): "Teach me Your way, O Lord; I will walk in Your truth; unite my heart to fear Your Name."
Mesillat Yesharim 26:1:
An Explanation of the Trait of Holiness
The matter of holiness is twofold: its beginning is service and its end is reward; its beginning is effort and its end is a gift. That is, its beginning is what a person sanctifies himself, and its end is what he is made holy. This is what they said, of blessed memory (Yoma 39a): a person who sanctifies himself a little is made holy a great deal; sanctifies himself from below, he is made holy from above.
Mesillat Yesharim 26:2: The effort is that a person should be entirely separated and removed from materiality, and always cleave, at every time and every hour, to his God. And in this vein the prophets were called angels, as in the matter said of Aaron (Malachi 2:7): "For the lips of the priest should keep knowledge, and they should seek the Torah at his mouth, for he is the messenger of the Lord of Hosts." And it says (II Chronicles 36:16): "But they mocked the messengers of God, etc." And even at the time of his engaging in the physical activities necessitated by his body, his soul does not move from its supernal cleaving, in the vein of the verse (Psalms 63:9): "My soul cleaves after You; Your right hand upholds me."
Mesillat Yesharim 26:3: And indeed, since it is impossible for a person to place himself in this state by his own effort alone, for it is too heavy for him — since in the end his substance is flesh and blood — therefore I said that the end of holiness is a gift; for what a person can do is make the effort of pursuing true knowledge and persisting in reflection on the holiness of his deeds,
Mesillat Yesharim 26:4: but the end result is that the Holy One, blessed be He, guides him along this path which he desires to walk, and causes His holiness to rest upon him and sanctifies him; and then this thing will succeed in his hand, that he can be in this constant cleaving with Him, blessed be He.
Mesillat Yesharim 26:5: For what nature withholds from him, He, blessed be He, will help him and grant him assistance, in the vein of the verse (Psalms 84:12): "He will not withhold good from those who walk in innocence."
Mesillat Yesharim 26:6: And therefore they said in the statement I mentioned: a person sanctifies himself a little — this is what a person can acquire through his own effort; he is made holy a great deal — this is the help that the Lord, blessed be He, gives him, as we have written.
Mesillat Yesharim 26:7: And behold, the man who is sanctified with the holiness of his Creator — even his physical deeds return to being matters of actual holiness; and your sign for this is the eating of sacred offerings, which is itself a positive commandment, and they said, of blessed memory (Pesachim 59b): the priests eat and the owners are atoned for.
Mesillat Yesharim 26:8: And you can now see the difference between the pure person and the holy person: the pure person's physical deeds are for him only a necessity, and he himself does not intend them except for the sake of necessity, so that through this he removes himself from the category of evil that is in materiality and remains pure; but he has not yet come to the category of holiness, for if it were possible without them, that would already have been better.
Mesillat Yesharim 26:9: But the holy person, always cleaving to his God, whose soul walks among true understandings in love and fear of his Creator — behold, it is accounted to him as though he walks before the Lord in the lands of the living, while still here in this world.
Mesillat Yesharim 26:10: And behold, such a man is himself accounted as the Tabernacle, as the Temple, and as the Altar, as our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Bereishit Rabbah 47:8): "and God went up from him" (Genesis 35:13) — the Patriarchs, they themselves are the Chariot. And so they said (Rashi, Genesis 35:13): the righteous, they themselves are the Chariot.
Mesillat Yesharim 26:11: For the Divine Presence rests upon them just as it rested in the Temple. And from now on, the food that they eat is like a sacrifice that ascends upon the fire-offerings, for it is certainly to be accounted a great elevation for those very things that used to ascend upon the altar, since they were offered before the Divine Presence.
Mesillat Yesharim 26:12: And they had so great an advantage in this that their entire species was blessed throughout the world, as our Sages, of blessed memory, said in the Midrash. So too, the food and drink that the holy man eats is an elevation for that food and that drink, as though it were truly offered upon the altar. And this is the matter of which they said, of blessed memory (Ketubot 105b): whoever brings a gift to a Torah scholar is as though he had offered the first fruits. And so they said (Yoma 71a): let the throat of Torah scholars be filled with wine in place of libations.
Mesillat Yesharim 26:13: And this does not mean, God forbid, that Torah scholars should be avidly pursuing eating and drinking, filling their throats like one who force-feeds a glutton; rather, the matter is according to the intention I have mentioned, for Torah scholars, holy in their ways and in all their deeds, are truly like the Temple and like the Altar, because the Divine Presence rests upon them just as it truly rested in the Temple; and what is offered to them is like what is offered upon the altar, and the filling of their throats stands in place of the filling of the libation basins.
Mesillat Yesharim 26:14: And in this vein, any use they make of worldly things, once they are already bound up with His holiness, blessed be He, is an elevation and an advantage for that thing, that it merited to be of service to the righteous man; and our Sages, of blessed memory, already mentioned this regarding the stones of the place that Jacob took and set under his head (Chullin 91b): Rabbi Yitzchak said, this teaches that they all gathered together, and each one was saying, "Let the righteous one rest his head upon me."
Mesillat Yesharim 26:15: The general rule of the matter: the matter of holiness is that a person should cleave so entirely to his God that in no deed that he performs will he separate or move away from Him, blessed be He — to the point that the physical things which serve him in his use of them are elevated more by his use of them than he himself descends from his cleaving and his rank by making use of physical things.
Mesillat Yesharim 26:16: And indeed this comes about when his mind and understanding are always fixed on His greatness, blessed be He, and His loftiness and His holiness, until he is found to be truly joined to the supernal angels while still in this world.
Mesillat Yesharim 26:17: And I have already said that a person cannot bring this about on his own, but only be aroused to the matter and strive toward it; and this is after all the good traits we have mentioned up to now, from the beginning of watchfulness to fear of sin, are already found in him — through this he will come to holiness and succeed, for if the earlier ones are lacking in him, he is like a stranger and one blemished, of whom it is said, "and a stranger shall not come near" (Numbers 18:4).
Mesillat Yesharim 26:18: But after he has prepared himself with all these preparations, if he increases his cleaving with the strength of love and the intensity of fear, through understanding His greatness, blessed be He, and the intensity of His loftiness, he will separate himself from matters of materiality little by little, and in all his activities and all his movements, he will direct his heart toward the innermost secrets of true attachment, until a spirit from on high is poured upon him, and the Creator, blessed be He, causes His Name to dwell upon him, as He does for all His holy ones.
Mesillat Yesharim 26:19: And then he will be truly like an angel of the Lord, and all his deeds, even the lowly and physical ones, will be like sacrifices and services.
Mesillat Yesharim 26:20: And you can see that the way to acquire this trait is through much abstinence, and immense reflection on the secrets of supernal providence and the mysteries of creation, and knowledge of His grandeur, blessed be He, and His praises, until he cleaves to Him with a great cleaving and knows how to direct his thought while going about and making use of earthly ways — just as it was fitting for the priest to have proper intention while slaughtering the offering, or receiving its blood, or sprinkling it, so that through this he would draw down from Him, blessed be He, blessing, life, and peace.
Mesillat Yesharim 26:21: And without this it is impossible for him to attain this rank, and he will remain, in any case, material and physical like all other people.
Mesillat Yesharim 26:22: Now, what helps in the attainment of this trait is solitude and much abstinence, so that in the absence of distractions his soul can grow stronger and cleave to the Creator.
Mesillat Yesharim 26:23: The things that undermine this trait are a lack of true knowledge and excessive company with people, for materiality finds its own kind and is awakened and strengthened, and the soul remains trapped in it and does not escape its imprisonment.
Mesillat Yesharim 26:24: But when he separates himself from them and remains alone, and prepares himself for the resting of His holiness, then, on whatever path he wishes to walk, they will lead him; and with the divine help that will be given him, his soul will grow strong within him and overcome physicality, and will cleave to His holiness, blessed be He, and become complete in it.
Mesillat Yesharim 26:25: And from there he will ascend to a still higher rank, which is the Holy Spirit, when his understanding comes to be above the human standard.
Mesillat Yesharim 26:26: And his cleaving can reach so great a rank that the key of the resurrection of the dead is placed in his hand, as it was given to Elijah and Elisha — this being an indication of the intensity of his attachment to Him, blessed be He, since He, blessed be His Name, is the source of life, who gives life to every living thing. And as our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Ta'anit 2a): three keys were not entrusted into the hand of an agent — the key of the resurrection of the dead, etc. Behold, whoever cleaves to Him, blessed be He, with a complete cleaving, can draw from Him, blessed be He, even the flow of life itself, which is what is most particularly associated with Him, above all else, as I have written; and this is what the baraita concludes: and holiness leads to the Holy Spirit, and the Holy Spirit leads to the resurrection of the dead.
Mesillat Yesharim 26:27: And you, pleasant reader, know that, like me, you know that I have not exhausted in this book of mine all the laws of piety, and I have not said everything there is to say on this matter, for the matter has no end, and reflection has no limit.
Mesillat Yesharim 26:28: But I have said a little of each particular among the particulars of the baraita upon which I founded this composition of mine, which can serve as a beginning and a starting point for broadening the reflection on these matters, since their way has now been revealed and their path opened before our eyes, to walk in them on a straight road. And concerning all such matters it is said (Proverbs 1:5): "let the wise man hear and increase learning, and the man of understanding acquire wise counsel"; and whoever comes to purify himself is helped (Shabbat 104a), for "the Lord gives wisdom; out of His mouth come knowledge and understanding" (Proverbs 2:6), to guide each and every person on his way before his Creator.
Mesillat Yesharim 26:29: And this is simple, for every person, according to the craft in his hand and the occupation with which he is occupied, needs guidance and direction accordingly; for the way of piety fitting for one whose Torah is his craft is not the way of piety fitting for one who must hire himself out for his fellow's work, and neither of these is the way of piety fitting for one who engages in commerce, and so with all the other particulars found in people's worldly occupations — each one, according to what he is, has the ways of piety fitting for him; not that piety itself changes, for it is certainly the same for every soul, since it is nothing but doing what gives satisfaction to one's Maker.
Mesillat Yesharim 26:30: But since the subjects change, it is impossible that the means which bring them to the goal should not change as well, each according to its own matter. And a man whose mouth never ceases from study can indeed be a complete pious man, just as one who, out of necessity, works at a lowly craft; and it is written (Proverbs 16:4): "The Lord has made everything for His own purpose." And it says (Proverbs 3:6): "In all your ways know Him, and He will make your paths straight."
Mesillat Yesharim 26:31: May He, blessed be His Name, in His mercy, open our eyes through His Torah, and teach us His ways, and lead us in His paths, and may we merit to give honor to His Name and to give satisfaction before Him. May the glory of the Lord endure forever; may the Lord rejoice in His works (Psalms 104:31). Let Israel rejoice in his Maker; let the children of Zion be glad in their King (Psalms 149:2). Amen, Amen, Amen.
